reason: The cited evidence (E1) discusses thermal stress-induced cracking in an Al-HEA coating, not the native oxide on Q235 steel, and attributes cracking to internal stresses rather than thermal expansion mismatch. It provides no support for the key premises regarding Q235 steel's oxide behavior, corrosion mechanism, or the protective role of an intact film.
premises: Thermal stresses induce microcracking in the native oxide layer of Q235 steel at elevated temperatures.
Microcracking of the oxide film exposes fresh metal to aggressive species, triggering localized galvanic corrosion.
Differences in thermal expansion between the steel substrate and its oxide cause stress build-up.
An intact oxide film suppresses corrosion-related degradation.
